Halyard

Plan the week. Ship the week. A dark, keyboard-first system for product UI.

Design system · v0.1

Halyard

Halyard

Halyard is a design system for dark, keyboard-first product UI: one set of tokens, components and motion that builds both the marketing site and the app. It is quiet by default, with graphite surfaces and a single warm accent, and it uses motion to explain what changed.

The code lives in the @halyard/ui package (React + TypeScript, with Storybook). This folder is the reference: tokens, live component previews and the rules for using them.

Principles

  • One accent, used sparingly. hy-signal (amber) marks the one thing that matters in a view: what is new, live, recommended or focused. Everything else is greyscale.
  • Motion explains change. Indicators slide to the new choice, panels grow from where they open, a new row flashes once. Nothing moves only to decorate.
  • Complete at rest. Every animation ends at the default state, so a screen is fully readable with reduced motion or before scripts load.
  • Keyboard first. Every action is reachable by keyboard, common ones have single-key shortcuts, and everything lives in the ⌘K command menu.
  • Dense but calm. Small type and tight rows in the app; generous space and big type on marketing pages. Both share the same tokens.

Colour

  • Surfaces step up in three levels: hy-bg (page), hy-bg-raise (windows, bars, panels), hy-bg-card (cards). Separate them with hy-line hairlines rather than shadows.
  • Text has three levels: hy-fg for headings and primary text, hy-fg-2 for body and secondary, hy-fg-3 for IDs, captions and dates.
  • hy-signal once per view. Status colours only mean status: hy-ok in review, hy-info done, hy-danger blocked. hy-lavender is an extra categorical colour for projects and charts.
  • Dark is the primary theme. The light theme keeps the same roles; the accent darkens to #b8711a so it holds contrast on white.
  • Text on a filled accent or the primary button uses hy-fg-inverse.

Type

  • Geist for everything; Geist Mono for IDs, numbers, versions, eyebrows and keys. Both are free on Google Fonts.
  • Headings are Geist 600 in solid hy-fg with tight negative tracking (-0.045em at the largest size) and balanced wrapping. Never gradient, serif or italic.
  • Display sizes are fluid: display-lg is clamp(2.6rem, 7vw, 5.25rem), display-md clamp(2rem, 4.4vw, 3.3rem), display-sm clamp(1.6rem, 3vw, 2.25rem). The type specimens show their maximums.
  • Body is 16px at 1.55 line height, about 62 characters wide. Ledes are 17–19px in hy-fg-2, about 48 characters wide.
  • Eyebrows: Geist Mono 12px, uppercase, +0.08em tracking, in hy-signal, after an 18px rule.

Space and layout

  • 4px base. Lay out siblings with gap, never margins between them.
  • Content column: 1120px max with a 16px gutter at every width. App sidebar: 220px; it becomes a drawer under 860px.
  • Card grids use a 14px gap. Cards pad 26px. Sections pad 96px on desktop, 64px on mobile.
  • Radii by role: hy-radius-sm tabs and menu items, hy-radius-md buttons and inputs, hy-radius-lg cards, hy-radius-xl windows and tables, hy-radius-full pills and tags.

Motion

Two curves and four durations cover everything.

Name Value Use
ease-out cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1) Entrances, reveals, panels opening
ease-spring cubic-bezier(.34, 1.56, .64, 1) Things moving to a new place: indicators, thumbs, fanned cards
fast 150ms Hover colour, key presses
base 250ms Buttons, arrows, borders
slow 450ms Sliding indicators, drawers
slower 1000ms Page-load entrance
stagger 90ms Between items in a load sequence

Presets (CSS classes, or the Reveal component):

  • .hy-rise: on load, fades in from an 8px blur and 14px below. Stagger with --hy-i.
  • .hy-reveal: on scroll, fades from 25% and rises 24px. Scroll-driven, no JavaScript.
  • .hy-tilt-in: a product window flattening from an 18° tilt as it scrolls in.
  • .hy-grow-x: progress and timeline bars growing from the left.
  • .hy-flash: a single amber flash behind something that just appeared.

Rules: one orchestrated moment per screen (the hero entrance on marketing pages, the command menu in the app); move indicators instead of swapping them; wrap every animation in prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

Signature interactions

  • Sliding indicator: a soft pill behind the active nav link, tab or filter that springs to the new choice.
  • Cursor spotlight: cards glow under the pointer and their border lights up in amber nearby.
  • Command menu: ⌘K opens a frosted menu that scales in on the spring curve; typing filters; Enter runs.
  • Page transition: the old page fades out with a slight blur, the new one fades up; the header stays put.

Voice and copy

  • Plain and specific. Short sentences, active voice, sentence case everywhere.
  • Name things the way people recognise them: "notifications", not "webhook config".
  • Buttons are verbs that say what happens: "Start building", "Create issue". Confirmations echo them: "Issue created".
  • Errors say what went wrong and how to fix it, without apologising.
  • Numbers are real and specific ("48 ms", "6 pts left"), set in Geist Mono.

Iconography

  • There is no icon font yet. The product uses simple Unicode glyphs (＋ ↻ ◎ ◇ ▤ →) at text size in hy-fg-2, and drawn status and priority icons (StatusIcon, PriorityIcon).
  • When adding an icon set, use 1.5px strokes on a 16px grid with round caps, in currentColor, to match the mark.

Logo

The mark is an A-frame with an amber crossbar. Files and clear-space rules are in assets/logos/. In code use <Logo /> or <LogoMark />, which follow the theme.

Using it in code

  • Install the package and import @halyard/ui/styles.css once. Put class="hy-body" on <body>. Set data-theme="light" on <html> for the light theme.
  • Reference tokens as CSS variables: var(--hy-signal), var(--hy-space-4), var(--hy-radius-lg).
  • Build screens from the components first. App screens start from AppShell; global actions go in CommandMenu.
  • The repository includes Storybook, a GitHub Pages workflow for it, and an AGENTS.md that tells AI coding tools how to use the system.

Logo

Logos

The Halyard mark: an A-frame of two strokes with an amber crossbar.

  • halyard-mark-on-dark.svg: strokes in hy-fg dark value (#eceef2), crossbar in hy-signal (#f2b66d). Use on dark surfaces.
  • halyard-mark-on-light.svg: strokes #16181d, crossbar #b8711a. Use on light surfaces.
  • The wordmark is the mark plus "Halyard" set in Geist 600 at -0.02em tracking, 10px gap. In code use <Logo /> or <LogoMark />, which follow the theme automatically.
  • Minimum size 16px. Keep clear space equal to the crossbar length on every side. Never recolour the crossbar to anything but the signal accent.

Components

Live previews running the real components. Each one lists when and how to use it.

Containers

Accordion

Questions and answers, or any list of sections where people only need one or two open.

  • Panels expand by animating their height from zero; the plus turns into a minus.
  • One panel open at a time by default; pass multiple to allow several.
  • Closed panels are removed from the tab order.
Layout

AppShell

The full-height app layout: sidebar, sticky top bar and scrolling content.

  • Compose with Sidebar, SidebarSection, SidebarItem and Topbar.
  • Sidebar items show an icon or a coloured dot (teams, projects) and an optional count in mono.
  • Under 860px the sidebar becomes a drawer: pass sidebarOpen and onSidebarClose, and give Topbar an onMenu handler to show the menu button.
Content

Avatar

A person's initials in a coloured disc.

  • Pass name; the colour is picked from the name so the same person always gets the same colour.
  • xs 18px in activity feeds, sm 20px in rows, md 28px in quotes and headers.
  • The full name is the accessible label and tooltip.
Actions

Button

Triggers an action; one primary button per view, for the main next step.

  • primary: the single most important action (Start free, Create issue). Fill hy-btn-primary-bg, text hy-fg-inverse.
  • secondary (default): every other action. hy-bg-raise fill, hy-line-strong border.
  • ghost: low-emphasis actions in dense areas (Log in, toolbar actions).
  • arrow adds a trailing → that nudges 3px right on hover. Use it for actions that move the person forward.
  • Sizes: sm 30px (toolbars), md 36px (default), lg 40px (forms, plan cards).
  • For links use LinkButton, or buttonClass() on a router link.
  • Labels are verbs in sentence case: "Start building", not "Get Started Now".
Containers

Card

A bordered surface that groups one idea: a feature, a plan, an integration, a cycle.

  • spotlight (on by default) adds a soft glow under the cursor and lights the border nearby in hy-signal.
  • highlighted marks the one recommended item in a set (an amber border and faint top tint).
  • interactive lifts 2px on hover for clickable cards.
  • Cards in a row share padding and baselines; let content set the height.
Navigation

CommandMenu

The global action launcher, opened with ⌘K or Ctrl+K.

  • Every frequent action belongs here with its single-key shortcut.
  • Type to filter, arrows to move, Enter to run, Escape to close.
  • Opens with a spring scale from 96% and a fade; the scrim dims the page.
  • inline renders it without the overlay for docs and empty states.
Product

IssueRow

One work item in a list: priority, ID, status, title, label and assignee.

  • Wrap rows in IssueList. Titles truncate with an ellipsis; nothing else wraps.
  • In narrow containers (under 520px) the priority and label hide automatically.
  • flash highlights a row once in hy-signal-soft right after it is created.
Content

Kbd

Shows a keyboard key or shortcut.

  • sm inline in text and menus ("press ⌘ K"), lg as an illustration.
  • pressed animates a key press (2px drop, amber label). Use it to demonstrate shortcuts, never as a state.
  • Every command-menu item with a shortcut shows it with Kbd.
Marketing

Marquee

An endless horizontal strip, used for customer names under a hero.

  • Edges fade out; it pauses on hover. With reduced motion it stops and wraps into centred rows.
  • Items are in hy-fg-3 and brighten on hover. Keep them all the same height.
Marketing

Pill

An announcement link at the top of a hero.

  • One short sentence plus an optional solid badge ("New", "Beta"). The arrow nudges right on hover.
  • Link it to the changelog entry or page that explains the news.
Product

PriorityIcon

Three rising bars; the number of lit bars is the priority (0 to 3).

  • Sits at the start of an issue row. Lit bars use hy-fg-2, unlit hy-line-strong.
Product

ProgressBar

A 6px bar for how much of a cycle, project or upload is complete.

  • signal for the live or current item, info for others, ok for review stages.
  • animateOnScroll grows the bar from zero as it enters the viewport.
  • Always give it a label.
Motion

Reveal

Applies the system's motion presets to any element.

  • mode="load" with index: the hero entrance, blur plus 14px rise, staggered 90ms. Use once per page.
  • mode="scroll" (default): fades from 25% and rises 24px as the element enters the viewport.
  • mode="tilt": a product window that flattens from an 18° tilt as it scrolls in; give the parent perspective: 1600px.
  • Everything ends at the resting state, so content is complete with reduced motion or no JavaScript.
Inputs

SegmentedControl

Switches between two to four views of the same thing (Monthly/Annual, Sign up/Log in, List/Board).

  • The thumb slides to the chosen option with the spring curve, 450ms.
  • Options share equal width. Keep labels to one or two words.
  • Use Tabs instead when choosing between sections or pages.
Product

StatusIcon

A 14px circle that shows where an issue is in the workflow.

  • todo: outline. in-progress: half filled in hy-signal. in-review: three-quarters in hy-ok. done: solid hy-info. canceled: grey with a strike.
  • Always pair with the text label somewhere on screen, or rely on its built-in accessible label.
Containers

Table

A native table styled to the system, inside a bordered panel that scrolls sideways on small screens.

  • Header row sits on hy-bg-raise and stays visible while scrolling.
  • Group rows (TableGroupRow) use the mono eyebrow style.
  • TableCheck renders ✓ in hy-fg and — in hy-fg-3, each with an accessible label.
  • Numbers use tabular figures.
Navigation

Tabs

Navigation and filters with a sliding indicator behind the active item.

  • plain for the site nav, sticky sub-navs and scroll-spy day lists; track for filters inside a bordered track.
  • orientation="vertical" for side navigation within a page.
  • Items with href render as links with aria-current="page"; others as toggle buttons.
  • The indicator moves to the new item rather than appearing there. Pass value={null} to hide it (no page active).
Content

Tag

A short label for a category or state, one or two words.

  • neutral for categories (Bug, Feature). Tones only mean status: signal live/new, ok in review, info done, danger blocked.
  • solid for one high-emphasis label per view, like "New" in an announcement pill.
  • dot adds a leading dot in the tone colour; use it in lists where the colour carries meaning.
Inputs

TextField

A labelled single-line input with an optional hint or error.

  • The label is always visible; placeholders show an example, never the label.
  • Focus shows an amber border and a soft hy-signal-soft halo.
  • Errors say what went wrong and how to fix it, in hy-danger, and are linked to the input for screen readers.
Foundations

Typography

Heading, Text and Eyebrow apply the type scale so screens never set sizes by hand.

  • Heading level 1 to 4 maps to display-lg, display-md, display-sm and card-title. Override the look with size when the outline needs a different level.
  • Headings are always Geist 600 in solid hy-fg, with tight negative tracking and balanced wrapping. No gradients, serif or italic words.
  • Text defaults to body in hy-fg-2; size="lede" for intros; mono for IDs and numbers.
  • Eyebrow labels a section: mono, uppercase, hy-signal, after an 18px rule.
